title: Belshazzar’s Feast
voicePrompt: In your own words, explain how this chapter narrates the fall of Babylon — Belshazzar's impious feast, the writing on the wall, Daniel's interpretation, and the night Babylon passed to the Medes and Persians. Why does Smith frame it as the prophesied transition from the gold to the silver of chapter 2?

questions.stem: According to Smith, what is the chief feature of interest in this chapter regarding prophetic history?
options: It describes the closing scenes of the Babylonish empire — the transition from the gold to the silver of chapter 2 and from the lion to the bear of chapter 7
It introduces Daniel's vision of the ram and the he-goat
It records Nebuchadnezzar's seven years of madness among the beasts
It predicts the rise of the little horn out of the Roman empire
questions.explanation: Smith states the chief feature is that it 'describes the closing scenes of the Babylonish empire, the transition from the gold to the silver of the great image of chapter 2, and from the lion to the bear of Daniel's vision in chapter 7.'

questions.stem: What act of impiety did Belshazzar commit while heated with his wine, according to Smith?
options: He ordered the temple in Jerusalem to be burned
He called for the sacred vessels taken from Jerusalem so he and his lords could drink from them while praising their heathen gods
He demanded that Daniel be executed for refusing to bow
He set up a golden image and commanded all to worship it
questions.explanation: Smith notes that 'when he began to be heated with his wine, [he] called for the sacred vessels which had been taken from Jerusalem,' and 'while they drank wine from vessels dedicated to the true God, they praised their gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone.'

questions.stem: How does Smith explain why Nebuchadnezzar is called Belshazzar's 'father' when he was actually his grandfather?
options: It was a scribal error introduced into the text
Belshazzar was legally adopted by Nebuchadnezzar
It followed the common custom of calling any paternal ancestor 'father' and any male descendant 'son'
Nebuchadnezzar and Belshazzar were brothers, not father and son
questions.explanation: Smith writes that Nebuchadnezzar 'is here called Belshazzar's father, according to the then common custom of calling any paternal ancestor, father, and any male descendant, son. Nebuchadnezzar was in reality his grandfather.'

questions.stem: Why, according to Smith, did Daniel refuse the king's gifts and rewards before interpreting the writing?
options: He wished it understood that he did not undertake the interpretation for the sake of gifts and rewards, unlike the soothsayers and astrologers
He believed accepting payment from a heathen king was forbidden by Jewish law
He intended to flee Babylon before the city fell and could not carry the gold
He had already been promised a greater reward by Cyrus
questions.explanation: Smith explains Daniel 'first of all disclaims the idea of being influenced by such motives as governed the soothsayers and astrologers... He wishes it distinctly understood that he does not enter upon the work of interpreting this matter on account of the offer of gifts and rewards.'

questions.stem: What does Smith consider the most likely explanation for why the king's wise men could not read the inscription, but Daniel could?
options: The writing was in Chaldaic, which only Daniel had been trained to read
The writing was upside down, and only Daniel thought to turn it around
It was a character strange to all parties, specially made known to Daniel by the Spirit of the Lord
The wise men were drunk and could not focus their eyes
questions.explanation: Smith reasons that if it had been Chaldaic the wise men could have read it, and after mentioning Dr. Clarke's conjecture concludes: 'It seems much more likely that it was a character strange to all the parties, and that it was specially made known to Daniel by the Spirit of the Lord.'

questions.stem: What do the words MENE, TEKEL, and PERES (UPHARSIN) signify in Daniel's interpretation?
options: Glory, honor, and majesty given to the king
Numbered (kingdom finished), weighed (found wanting), and divided (given to the Medes and Persians)
Mercy, judgment, and restoration promised to Babylon
Gold, silver, and brass representing three coming kingdoms
questions.explanation: Smith gives the interpretation: 'Mene, numbered; Tekel, weighed; Upharsin, from the root peres, divided' — God has numbered the kingdom's days and finished it, the king is weighed and found wanting, and the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

questions.stem: According to Smith, how did the Persian army actually enter Babylon on the night the city fell?
options: They scaled the brazen gates under cover of darkness
They bribed the watchmen to open the palace doors
They came through the emptied channel of the Euphrates into the heart of the city
They tunneled beneath the city walls over many weeks
questions.explanation: Smith describes that 'the Persian soldiery, through the emptied channel of the Euphrates, had made their way into the heart of the city, and were speeding forward with drawn swords to the palace of the king.'

questions.stem: Why does Smith suggest Daniel accepted the position of third ruler in the kingdom even after pronouncing its doom?
options: Because he hoped to overthrow Belshazzar and seize the throne for himself
Probably with a view to be better prepared to look after the interests of his people during the transition to the succeeding kingdom
Because the queen mother commanded him to accept it
Because he wished to keep the scarlet robe and gold chain as proof of his prophecy
questions.explanation: Smith writes that Daniel accepted the honor 'probably with a view to be better prepared to look after the interests of his people during the transition to the succeeding kingdom.'
